title: Inline-editing a `password` / `secret` field on the detail page renders the mask as the value and writes it straight back
body:
Filed unassigned per Prime Directive #10, from the fall-through sweep for #4216. Split out from #4220 (the rest of that sweep) because the severity and the argument are different: this one writes a masked placeholder into a credential field.

## What happens

`packages/plugin-detail/src/InlineFieldInput.tsx` has no branch for `password` or `secret`, so both reach the terminal raw text input at the end of the component. The detail hosts' editability gate (`DetailSection` / `HeaderHighlight`) excludes only readonly, computed and system fields, so neither type is held back: the pencil / double-click affordance appears on a credential field.

Both types are **masked on read**. The value the cell holds is therefore a placeholder, not the secret — so the inline editor seeds a plain text box with the mask, shows it in clear as if it were the current value, and saves it back verbatim if the user commits the row.

## This decision is already written down, one package over

`@object-ui/fields` excludes both from in-place editing and gives exactly this reasoning — `INLINE_EXCLUDED_FIELD_TYPES` in `FieldEditWidget.tsx`:

> Credentials — never inline-editable. Both are masked on read, so the cell has no real value to seed an editor with, and the grid's fallback is a PLAIN TEXT input: it would render the mask as if it were the value and write it straight back. `secret` additionally round-trips through an encrypted store (ADR-0100, data/field.zod.ts) — the cell holds an opaque ref, not the secret.

The grid honours that set. `InlineFieldInput` never consults it, so the detail page reproduces the exact failure the set exists to prevent — including, for `secret`, writing a mask over what should be an opaque reference into an encrypted store.

## Why it is not "just" a corrupted field

Two distinct harms beyond the overwrite:

1. **Disclosure shape** — the mask is rendered in a `type="text"` input, so whatever the mask contains is displayed in clear and is selectable/copyable, in a control the user believes holds their credential.
2. **Silent credential loss** — committing the row replaces a working secret with the placeholder, and nothing in the flow says so. The failure surfaces later, wherever that credential is used.

## Likely shape of a fix

Make both non-editable inline on the detail path, by the same rule the grid uses — have the hosts' editability gate consult `isInlineExcludedFieldType()` from `@object-ui/fields` rather than growing a second hand-maintained list. Pin it: a `password` and a `secret` field must render no inline-edit affordance and must not produce an editor. Re-authoring a credential belongs in the record form, which has the widget for it (`PasswordField`).

Related: #4220 (the remaining fall-through classes and the `FieldEditWidget` duplication behind all of them), #4219 (`autonumber` slipping the computed gate), #4216 (the object-valued composites).
